before: The association kultur.im.puls was founded in 2009 and runs the Galerie im Stiegenhaus in the staircase of the Impuls Center in Seeboden, with a second exhibition space in the stairwell of the Seeboden municipal office. Carolin Meinl has chaired it since 2024; Peter Kleinfercher, owner of the Impuls Center, is its honorary chairman. Besides the exhibitions it organises “Kunst am Abend”, poetry slams, painting Saturdays and an art lending library (Artothek). Source: kultur-impuls.com, impulscenter.at.

The Volkskino at Kinoplatz 3 in Klagenfurt shows current films, film classics, silent films and original-language versions, and offers screenings for schools. The federal funding list for programme cinemas for 2026 names it as “Alternativkino Klagenfurt, Neues Volkskino”. In 2026 the cinema marks 100 years of the Volkskino. Source: volkskino.at, bmwkms.gv.at.

The Universität Klagenfurt was founded in 1970. It has four faculties and 30 institutes, with more than 13,300 students. Its Institute of Instructional and School Development (Institut für Unterrichts- und Schulentwicklung) belongs to the Faculty of Cultural and Educational Sciences. Source: aau.at.

The Kulturinitiative bewegung / movimento / gibanje IN kultur (short: bewegungINkultur) is based in Klagenfurt and names itself in German, Italian and Slovenian. Since 2015 it has kept up friendly and cultural contacts with artists and organisations in Friuli and Slovenia, above all with the Gruppo artistico culturale Albrecht Dürer in Tavagnacco near Udine, the artists' association DABLO in Goriška Brda and the Circolo Culturale ENDAS in Monfalcone. With them it organises bilateral and trilateral exhibitions in Carinthia, Friuli and the Slovenian Littoral.

In Klagenfurt the initiative shows its three-country exhibitions in the Studiogalerie of the Stadthaus, since 2024 under the title Trigeniale. Since 2018 it has run the exhibition series “Kunst in den Hügeln – Umetnost v Brdih – Arte nel Collio” at the Kmetija Moro winery in Vipolže, Goriška Brda, where artists from Carinthia exhibit. It also organises cultural trips to castles, palaces and exhibitions in Friuli and Slovenia. Its contact person and main organiser is Gerhard Lepicnik. Source: artist sheet of Trigeniale 26 (bewegungINkultur), meinbezirk.at, novice.at.

The Climate Fund Klagenfurt was set up in 2025 as an association within the EU project Climate Funding 4 Cities. It raises money for climate protection and climate adaptation projects in the greater Klagenfurt area; the projects are chosen in regular idea competitions run by the Smart Climate Lab, the city's citizen office for climate matters. In the first round, in spring 2025, a jury selected seven projects, funded with about 32,000 euros. Source: smartclimatelab.at.

The kärnten.museum is the museum of cultural history and natural science of the State of Carinthia. Its history begins in 1844 with the founding of the Geschichtsverein für Kärnten; the main building, the Rudolfinum at Museumgasse 2 in Klagenfurt, opened on 10 July 1884. After water damage in 2014 and a general renovation from 2020, the museum reopened on 21 November 2022 under the name kärnten.museum, formerly Landesmuseum Kärnten. Its hands-on museum for children and young people, the wissens.wert.welt, visits schools across Carinthia with the kidsmobil. Source: de.wikipedia.org, wissenswertwelt.at.

The Lebenshilfe Region Knittelfeld began on 3 February 1982 as a parents’ association and today is a non-profit company with its association behind it, chaired by Johann Hubmann. Nearly 100 people work in its workshops, homes and mobile services for people with intellectual disabilities. It is a member of the Lebenshilfe network in Austria. In the shop “Ideenreich” at Hauptplatz 17 it sells products made in its workshops. Source: lebenshilfe-knittelfeld.at, lebenshilfe.at, ideenreich-knittelfeld.at, meinbezirk.at.

The Kunstverein postWERK is a non-profit art association based in Villach, founded in 2012 by Dorothee Unkel, its honorary president. Barbara Ambrusch-Rapp has chaired it since January 2020. Members and guest artists show an annual exhibition on a yearly theme, in 2026 “FRAGIL” at the Dinzlschloss in Villach. Source: postwerk.at.
JUMP DOME Klagenfurt is a trampoline park of more than 5,000 m² at Magazingasse 14 in Klagenfurt. It opened in May 2021. Source: jumpdome.at.
